findings.finding: The opening says the team partly replicated the planning findings, names what the original found, and the abstract pairs representative successes with three changed threshold crossings and the extreme-setting rejection-rate discrepancy.

“We partly replicated the planning findings of Kupzyk (2011)” introduces the composite result. Sentence 2 gives the exact replay boundary. The following sentences distinguish the recurred ranking, adjusted empirical grid and sign count from the threshold and extreme-rate discrepancies.

The first sentence says the headline findings partly replicated. The same paragraph describes fresh rather than replayed estimates, gives both main positive comparisons and exceptions, and precedes the background on page 2.

“We partly replicated Kupzyk’s headline findings” precedes the fresh-sampling and exact-replay boundary, the within-grid mean losses, the common skew rebound, 51 of 54 exact thresholds and the 41 versus 40 counts.
The text defines formulaic, exemplary and empirical power before interpreting them and explains the contrasts in prose. Evidence links and disagreement IDs supplement the explanation.
The distinct numerical and source regeneration routes are described with commands, scope and prerequisite pointers.
The printed-precision classification and limited reconstruction scope are explained before the table and remain distinct from statistical uncertainty and the first-page scientific verdicts.

findings.location: Table 1, ICC row; compare p. 1 introduction and p. 2 section 2
findings.finding: Putting the published decline statement opposite only the rerun's .56 to .62 pp skew-size rebound reads as a source-versus-rerun disagreement. The introduction and section 2 report that the original Table 1 also has a rebound (.6098 to .6673 pp), so the page 1 headline row should explicitly attribute it on the published side while distinguishing it from the source prose.

Source printed p. 96, Table 4, actually rounds the skewed-size loss to .6 and .7 pp at .10 and .15. Recalculation from Table 1 gives .6098 and .6673 pp. The statement that loss declines is a contradiction between Kupzyk’s prose and his table. The same rebound occurs in the rerun (.5614 to .6248 pp).

A reader can trace the crossed grids, formulaic rules, planning contrasts, cluster thresholds, empirical/exemplary gap, Appendix C parameters and both Appendix D settings to distinct evidence. Completeness against the packet remains for the evidence phase.

Verified matched contrasts, relative ordering, one final normal-size sign change (five in the initial empirical grid), threshold 51/54 with changes at cells 11/13/54, and the maximum excess of eight versus seven.

All six participant-loss cases and the adverse 19-cluster source value are discussed; the 12 observation-loss rules and the 230-versus-236 completer calculation remain separate. The four factors and fresh random samples carry into p. 4.

The formulaic reference changes, 25,600 draws per cell, 54 adjusted empirical matches, two ordinary-band exceptions, 51 readable initial exemplary points, 54 final points and 18 deterministic precision matches agree with the results.

findings.location: §4, empirical gap, paired baseline, and Appendix C
findings.finding: The below-count and baseline difference distinguish the published full count from 51 readable pairs. The 50,000 paired fixed/refit comparison and its standard error match the evidence. All 324 Appendix C means stay within proxy-variance adjusted bands.
The null settings, denominator sweep, printed screen gaps, precision draw counts and independent Figure 4 demonstration have their own results and boundaries.
The observed-count df extension, realized versus averaged mask estimands, and the proxy for unknown Appendix C source Monte Carlo errors are explicit.

The source software/fit state, masks, rates and interval procedure are characterized separately. The denominator sensitivity and adverse-mask checks are treated as plausible explanations, with discriminating original records identified.

The central mask interval excludes the source value at 19 clusters; a separate adverse-mask diagnostic establishes feasibility. Available-observation calculations retain pre-dropout measurements and leave completer-only power outside scope.
Three initial exemplary markers are hidden. The fixed/refit difference addresses only one baseline, and the independent estimands leave universal equivalence unresolved.
Effective denominator, original fitted state, Optimal Design implementation, toy generator and streams remain unresolved.

The manuscript identifies which model, setting, targets and size schedules came from the dissertation and which extraction, generator reconstruction, independent checks and comparisons the replication performed.

findings.location: section 4, paired baseline and Appendix C paragraphs
findings.finding: The manuscript distinguishes fixed-covariance and refitted estimates on the same outcomes and explains why additional draws reduce uncertainty around each probability.

findings.location: Appendix A, Routes R and S and rebuild
findings.finding: Route R performs new simulation, comparison and numerical reconstruction from checked-in transcriptions. Route S handles the separate archival source. The report build consumes saved results.

findings.location: subtitle and abstract opening; p. 12 reference
findings.finding: The subtitle identifies the longitudinal cluster trial study and the abstract attributes the findings to Kupzyk (2011). It states the loss ranking, lowest-ICC result, eight-cluster maximum and usual empirical deficit before reporting rerun outcomes. The references identify the exact dissertation.

Citation kupzyk2011 matches the cover and formal title page of the 143-page archival copy: Kevin A. Kupzyk, 2011, The Effects of Simplifying Assumptions in Power Analysis, University of Nebraska–Lincoln, institutional record 106. The original abstract (printed p. ii) supports loss ordering and the lowest-ICC result; printed pp. 97–98 and 106–107 support the maximum and below-count claims.

findings.location: Table 1, signed effect, effect magnitude and direction columns, and note
findings.finding: The table lists both signed values for each of the eight rows, direction, relative magnitude, units/reference definitions, rounding tolerances and a separation from uncertainty and equivalence. The count row is terse, but the note defines the signed values 14 and 13 as counts above half the cells and Published/Ours shows the underlying 41 and 40 of 54.

Averaging the matched Table 1 differences gives the five source signed estimates 1.327, 4.391, 6.409, .454 and .851 pp. The paired rerun gives 1.275, 4.472, 6.443, .438 and .778. Source powers are printed to five probability decimals, so each contributes .0005 pp to the pair and averaging preserves the .001 pp bound.

The difference of 15% dropout loss at ICC .05 and .15 is 3.037 versus 3.062 pp. Subtracting two loss means gives the declared .002 pp bound. This scalar is distinct from the skewed-size rebound in the findings cells.

findings.location: Table 1, last two rows and note
findings.finding: Maxima above the between–within reference are 8 and 7 clusters. The count contrast subtracts the exact half-grid count (27) from 41 and 40, yielding 14 and 13 cells. Both use the printed integer half-unit tolerance .5. All eight pairs keep direction. Magnitudes track the stated rounding bounds and the note separates point estimates from equivalence.

findings.location: Table 1, Published and Ours cells in ICC row
findings.finding: The Published cell includes the stated decline and peak but omits the published table-derived skew-size rebound; only Ours describes a rebound. The paper's own numerical source finding on p. 2 makes the asymmetric presentation materially misleading.

findings.location: Table 1, loss, maximum count and below-count rows
findings.finding: The cells distinguish the published and reconstructed sides, report both values, and the note identifies the matched references, 0.5 integer tolerance and count origin. Evidence verification remains pending.
Source printed pp. 93–94 report the 1.3 pp mean at 5% interval dropout. The reconstructed 18-pair mean 1.274814 pp gives 1.27 pp in Ours.
Source printed pp. 93–94 report 4.4 pp for 15% interval dropout. The reconstructed 18-pair mean 4.471858 pp gives 4.47 pp.
Source printed p. 95 reports 6.4 pp for 70/30 allocation; the reconstructed 27-pair mean 6.443263 pp gives 6.44 pp.
Source printed pp. 95–96 report .45 pp for normally distributed sizes; the reconstructed .438215 pp matched mean gives .44 pp.
Source printed pp. 95–96 report .85 pp for negatively skewed sizes; the reconstructed .778279 pp matched mean gives .78 pp.

Both data sets peak at ICC .05. The observed .56 to .62 pp rebound is correct, but the Published cell omits the .61 to .67 pp rebound from Table 1 (.6 to .7 pp in Table 4), the evidence needed to understand why the partial verdict concerns the original prose claim.
Source Table 5 and printed p. 97 give up to eight extra clusters. The maximum rerun threshold excess is seven. The body names the three one-cluster moves.
Source printed p. 106 reports 41 of 54 below. The rerun gaps have 40 negative values among 54. The 39 of 51 readable source pairs in the body do not replace the original full-grid result.
